sunday 2nd like the manna in the desert, bread in plenty for the crowds is seen as a sign of
the coming of the kingdom and the heavenly banquet at the end of time. the actions of jesus
in the desert are described in the same way as his actions at the last supper; he takes, blesses,
tuesday 4th st john vianney (1786-1859) had to contend with poverty, military service and
his own intellectual shortcomings in order to become a priest. in 1817 he was sent to care for
the people of ars, a small french village. the marvellous gift of his seeing into the depths of
the soul brought the world to ars. from 1830 the curé averaged twelve to sixteen hours in the
confessional. patron of priests.
wednesday 5th dedication of the basilica of st mary major. in 431 the council of ephesus
declared that mary was the mother of god. very shortly after, this church was dedicated in
rome with the title of st mary, the first such church in the west.
first anniversary mass for john white at 10am.
thursday 6th the transfiguration . the cross requires the exodus of jesus, his death,
resurrection and glorification. the disciples have to realise that he must depart just as they
are now prepared for his going to jerusalem to die.
friday 7th st sixtus ii and his four deacons companions were put to death in 258.
blessing of the fleet at 4pm in greencastle.
saturday 8th st dominic (1170-1221) a spaniard who founded the order of preachers
(dominicans) to counteract the albigensian heresy
sunday 9th mass will be celebrated in ballinacrae.
the rosary and the divine mercy chaplet will be recited in st. pius x church, moville, at
7.30pm every day, from sunday – friday. adoration of the blessed sacrament on monday,
2-9pm; wednesday, 6-9pm.

sunday 26th listening to the word of god enables us to acquire true wisdom. by it we learn
where our true good lies, that it means more than silver and gold. this wisdom helps us to make
the right choices in our search for the real treasure. we ought to pray for the ability to make the
positive, radical decision for the kingdom. jesus asks us all, ‘have you understood all this?’
wednesday 29th saints martha, mary and lazarus welcomed jesus as a family friend, martha
generously offered him hospitality, mary listened attentively to his words and lazarus promptly
emerged from the tomb at the command of the one who humiliated death.
thursday 30th st peter chrysologus ‘of the golden word’, bishop and doctor of the church.
renowned for his preaching and pastoral zeal.
friday 31st st ignatius of loyola (1491-1556) came from the north of spain and founded the
society of jesus. by the time of his death, the society had spread widely and had over a thousand
members. his great theme was the service of god and god’s greater glory. the experience of his
conversion led to his writing of the spiritual exercises.
first anniversary mass for patricia white blouin at 10am in st pius x.
saturday 1st august st alphonsus liguori (1696-1786) is the founder of the redemptorist
congregation. he taught much on moral theology and the spiritual life. he is remembered as a
popular preacher and influential writer of theology.
mass in shrove oratory at 11am.
